title: 5 Centimeters Per Second
label: Quick read (from summaries)
premise: Yukiko Seike's manga adaptation of Makoto Shinkai's 2007 film follows Takaki Tono from childhood into adulthood. He and his close friend Akari are separated when her family moves, and their letters slowly thin out; later, classmate Kanae loves Takaki without being able to tell him. The manga extends the story, showing Kanae working as a nurse after the film's events.
life_message: Time and distance change people, and growing up means learning to carry first love as memory and move on.

Dignity vs honor.evidence: No confrontations; feelings are held inward.

Order vs freedom.evidence: Akari's parents forbid her staying in Tokyo; Takaki later drifts on his own path (Wikipedia).

Civic vs kin.evidence: Families move for parents' jobs; friendship and love matter more than clan.

Equality vs hierarchy.evidence: Peers and classmates; little hierarchy theme.

Tradition vs secular-rational.evidence: Modern, secular Japan of trains, letters and careers.

Survival vs self-expression.evidence: Inner feelings and personal meaning are the focus.

folkways.japan: Restraint in voicing feelings and frequent family relocations for work reflect common Japanese norms, and the story's mood draws on the aesthetic of mono no aware.

delivery.evidence: ANN review of the film says it 'never comes out and tells you what the characters are feeling'; manga delivery not reviewed (to verify).
delivery.note: The source film works through mood and imagery rather than stated themes; the manga is reported to follow it.

winners_losers: No one wins outright; the story sympathizes with all three young people and shows moving on as the hard, necessary path.
